author: Thorvardur de Shong
title: Uber Eats expands grocery lineup with five regional retail partners - NewsBreak
text:
By Thorvardur de Shong ,
8 hours ago SAN FRANCISCO – Uber Eats is expanding its grocery marketplace by adding five regional grocery retailers, giving shoppers more local options for online ordering and delivery.
The new partners include Busch’s Fresh Food Market, Hays, Lowe’s Market, Marc’s, and Piggly Wiggly locations in North Carolina. Customers can shop at the participating retailers through the Uber Eats, Uber, and Postmates apps, with access to on-demand or scheduled delivery and real-time order tracking.
The expansion strengthens Uber Eats’ grocery footprint and provides regional and independent grocers with another digital sales channel. The newly added banners span multiple states, including Michigan, Ohio, Texas, Arkansas, Missouri, and North Carolina.
“When it comes to grocery shopping, local preference matters,” said Hashim Amin, head of grocery and retail for North America at Uber. “Whether it’s a regional chain that has been part of a community for decades or a neighborhood market customers visit every week, people want familiar grocery options that fit their routines. These new partnerships help us bring more of those local favorites to Uber Eats while creating new opportunities for grocers to grow their business.”
Consumers can browse groceries, fresh produce, prepared foods, and household essentials from participating stores, choose delivery or scheduled fulfillment, and track orders in real time. Uber said that Uber One members will continue to receive a $0 delivery fee on eligible grocery orders.
